wasteRecycling.title: Curbside Waste, Recycling & Organics Collection
wasteRecycling.curbsidePlacementRule: All waste receptacles, blue recycling boxes, and green organic bins must be placed curbside by 7:00 AM on your scheduled collection day, and no earlier than 6:00 PM the evening prior.

missedCollectionPolicy.cutoffTime: Do not report a missed collection before 5:00 PM on your scheduled collection day. Collection trucks and municipal crews operate until 5:00 PM.
missedCollectionPolicy.lateSetoutNotice: If your bin was placed at the curb after 7:00 AM, crews are not required to return, and collection will take place on your next scheduled collection date.
missedCollectionPolicy.serviceLevelAgreement: Verified missed collections reported after 5:00 PM are resolved within 2 business days.

schedules.organicsGreenBin: Weekly collection year-round. Accepted: fruit and vegetable scraps, meat, bones, coffee grounds, soiled paper towels, pizza boxes.
schedules.recyclingBlueBox: Bi-weekly collection alternating with paper/cardboard and plastics/cans. Accepted: rigid plastics #1-#7, clean metal cans, paper, glass bottles.
schedules.garbage: Bi-weekly collection. Maximum limit of 2 standard bags/bins per household. Additional bags require a municipal Bag Tag ($3.00 each).

bulkPickup.schedule: First Tuesday of each calendar month.
bulkPickup.rules: Maximum 2 large items per household per month (e.g., sofas, appliances with Freon removed and certified tag). Mattresses must be fully encased in sealed plastic wrap.

wasteRecycling.hazardousWaste: Household Hazardous Waste (HHW) depot located at 450 Transfer Rd. Open Saturdays 9:00 AM – 3:00 PM. Never place batteries, paint, motor oil, or propane tanks in curbside bins.

illegalDumpingFAQ.question: Someone is illegally dumping waste in my neighborhood. What should I do?
illegalDumpingFAQ.answer: If actively in progress, call Police Dispatch at (555) 123-7623 or 911 immediately. Note vehicle make, license plate, and direction of travel without confronting the perpetrator. For discovered/abandoned waste, file a report on the 311 Citizen Portal (maplewoodnj.gov/services/request) or call DPW. Code enforcement officers inspect debris for identifying manifests. Under Township Code § 209-14, illegal dumping carries mandatory municipal court appearance, fines up to $2,500.00 per offense, cleanup restitution, and potential vehicle impoundment.

brokenParkBinFAQ.question: There is a broken garbage bin in the park. Can I report it?
brokenParkBinFAQ.answer: YES. Report via the 311 Citizen Portal under 'Park Infrastructure / Damaged Receptacle'. Specify the park name (e.g., Memorial Park, DeHart Park) and nearest landmark (e.g., tennis courts, playground entrance). DPW responds within 24 to 48 hours to repair or replace broken receptacles, and dispatches roving crews within 4 hours for overflowing weekend park bins.

garbagePilingFAQ.question: Garbage has been piling up near my house. Can I submit a complaint?
garbagePilingFAQ.answer: YES. Refuse accumulation violates Township Code § 209-7 and Property Standards Chapter 239. Submit a ticket on 311 or call Code Enforcement at (973) 762-8120 Ext. 3300. An officer conducts a site inspection within 24 hours and serves a formal 48-Hour Notice of Violation. If unabated, municipal crews clear the trash, and all costs plus administrative penalties are assessed as a tax lien against the property, alongside daily $250 court fines.

badSmellFAQ.question: There is a bad smell coming from a public garbage area. Can I report it?
badSmellFAQ.answer: YES. Report via 311 under 'Public Sanitation / Odor & Health Hazard'. DPW dispatches a sanitation crew within 24 hours to power-wash the receptacle with high-pressure hot water and hospital-grade biodegradable enzymatic deodorizer. Commercial dumpsters are inspected for tight-fitting lids and rodent-proof drain plugs under § 209-18.

potholeReporting.faqPotholeRequest: I want to create a service request for a pothole — what information do you need?
requiredInformation: 1. Exact Incident Location: Specific street address (e.g., '148 Valley Street') or primary road with nearest intersecting cross-streets (e.g., 'Baker St between Maplewood Ave and Ridgewood Rd').

2. Direction of Travel & Lane Position: Compass heading (Northbound, Southbound, Eastbound, Westbound) and exact lane (center travel lane, passenger-side tire track, driver-side track, parking gutter, or crosswalk).

3. Size & Depth Severity Bracket: Tier 1 (<25 cm / <10″ shallow pitting), Tier 2 (25–60 cm / 10–24″ standard pothole, 1–3″ deep), or Tier 3 (>60 cm / >24″ severe crater, >3″ deep with exposed sub-base gravel).

4. Road Jurisdiction Verification: Validation whether street is municipal or County roadway (Springfield Ave, Valley St, and Wyoming Ave are Essex County roadways routed to county dispatch with cross-reference tracking).
5. Environmental & Safety Hazards: Standing water concealing hole depth, sharp asphalt edges posing blowout risk, or bicycle/pedestrian lane obstruction.
6. Digital Photographs: Context photo showing roadway location plus close-up photo showing cavity depth and deterioration.
7. Reporter Contact Information: Full name, phone number (for SMS dispatch alerts), and email address to receive real-time case ID (CASE-2026-XXXX).
potholeReporting.reportingRequirements: Reports must provide the exact street address or closest cross-street intersection, travel lane direction, severity bracket, jurisdiction, safety conditions, photos, and citizen contact info.

sizeGuide.dimension: Under 25 cm (10 inches) diameter, depth under 5 cm (shallow surface spall)
sizeGuide.sla: Inspected and repaired within 5 business days

sizeGuide.dimension: 25 cm to 60 cm (10 to 24 inches) diameter, moderate depth 1–3 inches
sizeGuide.sla: Inspected and repaired within 3 business days

sizeGuide.dimension: Over 60 cm (24 inches) diameter or severe depth >3 inches (rim damage hazard)
sizeGuide.sla: Inspected and emergency patched within 24 hours (High severity)

potholeReporting.travelLaneRule: Any large pothole situated in an active travel lane, school zone, or bus corridor is flagged High Severity for immediate crew dispatch within 24 hours.
potholeReporting.duplicateDetectionThreshold: Existing reports within 50 meters submitted within the last 30 days are automatically consolidated into existing work orders to prevent duplicate crew dispatches while adding the citizen as an endorsed subscriber.

urgentSafetyProtocols.downedWiresNotice: CRITICAL HAZARD: If you observe downed power lines, stay back at least 10 meters (33 feet). Call Maplewood Hydro at 1-800-434-1235 or 911 immediately. Do NOT submit via standard web ticket.
urgentSafetyProtocols.fallenTreeOnRoad: If a fallen tree is actively obstructing vehicle traffic or touching overhead utility lines, call 911 and the 24/7 Road Dispatch at (555) 123-7623.

streetlights.reportingProcess: Provide the 6-digit pole identification tag (e.g., 'Pole ML-0412') located at eye level on the metal pole. Typical repair timeline is 5 to 7 business days.

parksForestry.title: Parks, Public Trails & Urban Forestry
parksForestry.parksInventory: Maplewood manages 18 public municipal parks, 35 kilometers of multi-use trails, 4 splash pads, 8 sports fields, and 1 dedicated off-leash dog park.

treeMaintenance.municipalResponsibility: The Town maintains all boulevard trees located within the municipal right-of-way (typically within 4.5 meters of the curb). Tree trimming near primary power lines is coordinated with electric utilities.
treeMaintenance.privateTrees: Trees situated entirely on private property are the legal responsibility of the property owner under By-law 2023-45 (Property Standards).

parksForestry.parkIssueReporting: Report damaged park benches, playground equipment defects, fallen branches, trail washouts, or graffiti. High-priority safety hazards are addressed within 24 hours.

waterServices.title: Municipal Drinking Water, Sewer & Quality
waterServices.waterSource: Drinking water is sourced from the Maplewood Aquifer and treated at the Central Water Purification Plant. Rigorous testing is conducted daily in accordance with provincial drinking water regulations.

conservationByLaw.rules: Lawn and garden watering permitted only on alternate days. Even-numbered municipal addresses may water on even calendar days; odd-numbered addresses on odd calendar days. Permitted hours are 6:00 AM – 8:00 AM and 7:00 PM – 9:00 PM only.

waterServices.emergencyWaterMainBreaks: Call (555) 123-9287 immediately for water main breaks, sudden drop in municipal water pressure, or discolored water notices.

snowRemoval.title: Winter Road Maintenance, Snow Emergencies & Plowing Routes

codeReferences.chapter257: Chapter 257 (Vehicles and Traffic), Article IV (Emergency No Parking) and § 257-36.7 / § 257-2.5
codeReferences.chapter239: Chapter 239 (Streets and Sidewalks), § 239-1 (Removal of snow and ice) and § 239-2 (Depositing snow in streets prohibited)

priorityPlowingSchedule.threshold: Cleared within 4 to 6 hours after 5 cm of snowfall accumulation. Includes Main St, Valley St, Springfield Ave, emergency hospital routes.
Cleared within 8 hours following snowfall completion. Includes neighborhood feeder roads and bus zones.
Cleared within 16 to 24 hours after 8 cm accumulation. Residential routes are plowed only once Priority 1 and 2 are fully maintained.

snowRemoval.overnightParkingBan: Under Municipal Code Chapter 257, on-street parking is strictly prohibited on all municipal streets between 2:00 AM and 6:00 AM. During winter snow events and declared States of Emergency, all on-street parking permits are suspended on snow-covered streets until plowing operations are concluded. Violations carry a $60 fine and mandatory vehicle towing.
snowRemoval.sidewalkClearingByLaw: Under § 239-1, residential and commercial property owners, tenants, and occupants are legally required to clear all snow and ice from abutting sidewalks within 24 hours following the end of snowfall. If ice cannot be removed, it must be thoroughly treated with salt or sand. Under § 239-2, throwing, shoveling, or plowing snow into already plowed public streets is strictly unlawful.
snowRemoval.towingAndImpoundPolicy: Under § 257-31, any unoccupied vehicle parked or standing in violation of emergency snow parking regulations is deemed a nuisance and a public menace. The Police Department is authorized to order immediate removal and impoundment. The registered owner is liable for all towing and daily storage fees prior to release.

animalControl.title: Animal Services, Pet Licensing & Wildlife
animalControl.licensingRequirements: All domestic dogs residing in Maplewood must be licensed annually before March 31. Cats must possess a valid microchip or collar tag.
animalControl.leashByLaw: Under By-law 2020-04, dogs must be kept on a physical leash no longer than 2.0 meters (6.5 feet) at all times in public spaces, parks, and sidewalks, except within the fenced perimeter of Maplewood Bark Park (42 River Valley Rd).
animalControl.lostFoundPets: Stray or found domestic animals are sheltered at the Maplewood Regional Animal Care Center. Contact Animal Control Dispatch at (555) 123-4567 ext. 240.

publicWorks.title: Department of Public Works (DPW) & Recycling Center

facility.name: Maplewood Department of Public Works Facility & Recycling Center

dualStreamRecycling.system: Dual-Stream Curbside Recycling (alternating weekly between Fibers and Commingled Containers)
dualStreamRecycling.fibersStream: Clean flattened cardboard, corrugated boxes, newspapers, magazines, junk mail, office paper, phone books, and brown paper grocery bags. Keep dry and bundle or place in bins.
dualStreamRecycling.commingledStream: Glass bottles and jars, aluminum cans, steel/tin food cans, and rigid plastic food/beverage containers stamped #1 through #7. Must be rinsed clean.
dualStreamRecycling.containerRequirements: Must be set out in hard plastic containers/tubs (maximum 64 gallons). Plastic bags of any kind are strictly prohibited in curbside recycling.

bulkDropOffProgram.overview: Biannual Saturday drop-off events held at the DPW Recycling Center (359 Boyden Ave) from 8:00 AM to 2:00 PM.
bulkDropOffProgram.eligibility: Township of Maplewood residents only. Proof of residency required: two forms of ID (photo driver's license and a recent utility or tax bill).
acceptedMaterials: Household furniture (sofas, sectionals, dressers, tables, desks, mattresses, box springs, lamps)
Large rigid plastics / MRPs (plastic playsets, outdoor patio furniture, large plastic bins, laundry baskets)
Non-freon household appliances and metal fixtures
Bicycles, luggage, and large household items
prohibitedMaterials: Building and construction materials (sheetrock, drywall, concrete, brick, lumber, roofing shingles, ceramic tiles, siding)
Kitchen cabinets, bathroom vanities, and porcelain sinks/toilets
Automotive parts, tires, and motor vehicle batteries
Paint cans, stains, chemical solvents, and toxic materials
Tree trunks, large stumps, and commercial landscape debris

seasonalLeafCollection.schedule: Four rotating collection rounds by municipal section conducted throughout October, November, and December.
guidelines: Rake leaves into the street along the gutter/curb by Sunday night prior to your section's collection week.
Do NOT put leaves out on municipal roadways more than 7 calendar days before your scheduled collection week.
Keep leaf piles strictly free from tree branches, rocks, stones, metal, or non-organic debris.
Never place leaves in plastic bags; bagged leaves will NOT be collected by DPW vacuum crews.
Gas-powered leaf blowers are strictly prohibited year-round in Maplewood under municipal environmental noise code.
seasonalLeafCollection.dropOffAlternative: Residents may haul and drop off leaves directly at the DPW yard (359 Boyden Ave) during regular operating hours.

springRakeOutProgram.schedule: Seasonal garden debris and spring cleanup service running from late March through April.
rules: Tree branches must be cut to lengths of 4 feet or less and securely tied with natural twine into bundles under 50 lbs.
Leaves, dead garden plants, and grass rakings must be contained in biodegradable paper yard-waste bags or reusable hard bins.
Loose debris left in street gutters during spring rake-out is strictly prohibited and subject to municipal fine.

streetSweeping.schedule: Residential and commercial streets are swept on scheduled bi-weekly rotations from April through November.
streetSweeping.parkingRestrictions: Temporary on-street parking prohibitions apply on designated sweeping days to enable curb-to-curb street sweeper clearance.

urbanForestryAndTreePermits.treeRemovalPermit: Under Township Tree Protection By-laws, a municipal Tree Removal Permit is mandatory prior to removing any healthy tree with a trunk diameter of 8 inches (20 cm) or greater on private property.
urbanForestryAndTreePermits.municipalTreeCare: DPW Forestry crews conduct ongoing pruning, safety assessments, and hazard removal for all trees on municipal road allowances, public parks, and rights-of-way.
urbanForestryAndTreePermits.freeArborDaySaplings: DPW hosts an annual Arbor Day free tree sapling giveaway for residents at the 359 Boyden Ave yard to replenish the urban tree canopy.

jitneyCommuterService.overview: Municipal commuter bus service transporting residents between residential neighborhoods and the Maplewood NJ Transit Train Station during peak weekday morning and evening commute windows.
jitneyCommuterService.passCost: $95.00 annual commuter pass, or individual tickets purchased at Town Hall and online.
jitneyCommuterService.fleetSustainability: Transition to 100% zero-emission electric jitney buses currently in deployment.

specialDisposalServices.freeMulchAndCompost: Free organic shredded wood mulch and screened leaf compost available for resident pickup at 359 Boyden Ave (self-load with own shovels and containers).
specialDisposalServices.electronicsEwaste: Electronic waste (computers, monitors, laptops, televisions, printers, phones) accepted year-round at the DPW Recycling Center.
specialDisposalServices.shredItEvents: Confidential paper document shredding events hosted semi-annually at the DPW yard (maximum 4 standard file boxes per household).

propertyTaxes.title: Property Tax Assessments & Mill Rates

distributionBreakdown.municipalPortion: 48% (Local roads, fire protection, parks, recreation, snow clearing, waste)
distributionBreakdown.regionalPortion: 34% (Public health, transit, emergency medical services, social housing)
distributionBreakdown.educationPortion: 18% (Local school boards as mandated by the province)

propertyTaxes.latePaymentPenalty: Interest and penalty of 1.25% per month is added on the first day of each calendar month following default, in accordance with the Municipal Act.

paymentMethods.instructions: Add 'Town of Maplewood - Property Taxes' as a payee through your online banking institution. Enter your 19-digit Assessment Roll Number without spaces or dashes.
Enroll in automatic withdrawals on the 1st of each month (10-month plan) or on statutory instalment due dates (4-instalment plan). No processing fee.
Visit Customer Service Counter at 123 Main Street. Accepted: Debit/Interac, Cash, Cheque, Money Order. Open Mon-Fri 8:30 AM – 4:30 PM.
Located outside the North Entrance of Town Hall (123 Main St). Cheques and stubs only; do not deposit cash.
Payable to 'Town of Maplewood'. Mail to: Revenue & Taxation, 123 Main Street, Maplewood, ON M4P 1T8.

preAuthorizedPlans.plan10Month: Monthly withdrawals deducted on the 1st day of each month from January to October. Accounts must be in good standing (zero arrears) to qualify.
preAuthorizedPlans.planInstalment: Automatic withdrawal processed on the exact instalment due dates: February 27, April 30, June 30, and September 30.
preAuthorizedPlans.enrollmentDeadline: Applications must be received at least 14 calendar days prior to the first requested withdrawal date along with a VOID cheque or direct debit form.

permits.notice: Permit information is intentionally minimal. For complete regulations, contact the Building Department at 123 Main St.

deckPermits.title: Residential Deck Permits

permitRequirementRules.exemptDecks: Certain low-profile freestanding decks may be exempt. Contact Building Dept for verification.
permitRequirementRules.mandatoryPermitDecks: Permits generally required for attached or elevated decks. Inquire at Town Hall.

deckPermits.zoningSetbacks: Standard property setbacks apply. Inquire with Building Department.
deckPermits.guardrailRequirements: Standard safety guardrails required for elevated walking surfaces.

poolPermits.title: Pool Enclosure Permits
poolPermits.mandatoryPermitRule: Permits may be required prior to installing residential pools or outdoor water features. Inquire at Town Hall.

fenceEnclosureSpecifications.minimumHeight: Standard enclosure height applies. Inquire with Building Department.
fenceEnclosureSpecifications.hotTubExemption: Locking safety covers may qualify for exemptions upon review.

burnPermits.title: Open-Air Burn Permits
burnPermits.zoningEligibility: Rural areas only. Inquire with Fire & Emergency Services.
burnPermits.fireBanRule: Open-air burning is prohibited during municipal fire bans.

buildingPermits.title: General Building Permits
buildingPermits.scope: Permits may be required for structural work, additions, and alterations. Inquire with Chief Building Official.

signagePermits.title: Commercial Signage
signagePermits.regulations: Commercial signage is subject to town sign by-law. Contact planning office.

burnPermit.title: Open-Air Burn Application
burnPermit.sla: Instant for verified agricultural parcel; 2 business days manual review

directFormsDirectory.title: Residential Deck Permit Application Form
directFormsDirectory.exactUse: Application for construction, structural repair, enlargement, or replacement of residential attached or detached decks, verandas, or porches over 24 inches (600 mm) in height.
requiredDetails: Site plan with property line setbacks (min 1.2m side, 6.0m rear)
Structural framing plans (beam size, joist span, 42-inch frost footings, railing details min 36 or 42 inches)
Contractor license & insurance or owner-builder declaration
directFormsDirectory.byLaw: Ontario Building Code & Township Code Ch. 120

directFormsDirectory.title: Swimming Pool & Hot Tub Enclosure Permit Application Form
directFormsDirectory.exactUse: Installation of in-ground pools, above-ground pools (water depth > 24 inches / 60 cm), outdoor swim spas, hot tubs, and mandatory perimeter safety enclosures/fences.
requiredDetails: Property boundary survey showing pool setbacks (min 1.5m from lot line)
Fence enclosure specifications (min 1.2m / 48" or 1.5m / 5ft, self-closing & self-latching gate swinging outward min 1.35m latch height)
Ontario One Call / Dig Locate confirmation

directFormsDirectory.title: Open-Air Agricultural Burn Permit Application Form
directFormsDirectory.exactUse: Controlled seasonal open-air burning of clean agricultural crop residues, woody brush, and orchard trimmings on eligible rural parcels. Strictly prohibited in urban/residential subdivisions.
requiredDetails: Confirmation of rural agricultural zoning & parcel size > 2.0 acres
On-site fire extinguishing equipment (charged 50-ft hose or 500-gal water tank)
Contact phone of adult supervisor (18+) present

directFormsDirectory.title: Central 311 Citizen Service Request Portal
directFormsDirectory.exactUse: Centralized municipal intake for all non-emergency civic work orders across roads, sanitation, parks, forestry, water utilities, and streetlights. Generates CASE-2026-XXXX tracking IDs.
directFormsDirectory.sla: Varies by category (24h to 5 business days)

directFormsDirectory.title: Pothole & Road Surface Hazard Request Form
directFormsDirectory.exactUse: Reporting potholes, asphalt craters, shoulder erosion, sunken catch basins, or road surface defects on municipal streets.
requiredDetails: Size tier (<25cm shallow, 25-60cm medium, >60cm emergency rim-damage crater)
directFormsDirectory.sla: 24 hours for Tier 3 / active travel lanes; 3–5 business days for standard Tier 1-2
directFormsDirectory.byLaw: Minimum Maintenance Standards for Municipal Highways (O. Reg. 239/02)

directFormsDirectory.title: Missed Curbside Waste & Bin Replacement Form
directFormsDirectory.exactUse: Reporting missed garbage, blue box recycling, green organics bin, or requesting replacement of broken curbside bins.
requiredDetails: Stream type (Garbage, Blue Box, Green Bin)
Confirmation bins set curbside before 7:00 AM
Must be reported strictly after 5:00 PM on collection day
directFormsDirectory.fee: Free Civic Service ($3.00 per surplus bag tag)

directFormsDirectory.title: Streetlight Outage & Damaged Fixture Repair Form

requiredDetails: 6-digit pole identification tag stamped on pole (format ML-XXXX, e.g. ML-0412)
directFormsDirectory.sla: 5 to 7 business days (24h for exposed wiring)

directFormsDirectory.title: Park Hazards, Broken Bins & Boulevard Tree Form

Specific landmark within park (e.g. playground, tennis courts)
Photo of damaged receptacle or hazard
directFormsDirectory.sla: Broken bins: 24 to 48 hours; Overflowing bins: 4 hours; Playground hazards: 48 hours

directFormsDirectory.title: Water Utility, Pressure & Meter Service Request Form

directFormsDirectory.fee: Standard banking processing; 1.25% monthly penalty on overdue balances
directFormsDirectory.sla: Instant receipt in person; 2–3 days for online banking

byLaws.title: Vehicles & Traffic Code: Snow Emergency Routes (§ 257-36.7 & § 257-2.5)
byLaws.summary: Establishes emergency no-parking restrictions on designated snow emergency routes upon declaration of emergency or snow-covered roadways. Authorizes immediate towing and impoundment of obstructing vehicles under § 257-31.

byLaws.title: Streets & Sidewalks: Snow & Ice Removal (§ 239-1 & § 239-2)
byLaws.summary: Mandates property owners and occupants clear sidewalks within 24 hours of snowfall cessation. Strictly prohibits plowing, shoveling, or blowing snow into public roadways that have already been cleared.

byLaws.title: Noise Control By-law
byLaws.summary: Prohibits construction noise between 7:00 PM and 7:00 AM on weekdays, and before 9:00 AM on Sundays and statutory holidays. Persistent canine barking and excessive amplified music prohibited at all times.

byLaws.title: Traffic & Winter Parking By-law
byLaws.summary: Establishes municipal speed limits, prohibited heavy truck routes, and the annual overnight winter parking ban (2:00 AM – 6:00 AM, Dec 1 – Mar 31).

byLaws.title: Property Standards By-law
byLaws.summary: Mandates maintenance of residential and commercial premises, long grass/weed control (maximum 20 cm height), exterior structural safety, and derelict vehicle prohibitions.

byLaws.title: Pool Enclosure By-law
byLaws.summary: Enforces perimeter safety fencing, minimum 1.5 m height, self-closing/latching gates for all residential pools and ponds deeper than 60 cm.

byLaws.title: Open-Air Burning By-law
byLaws.summary: Regulates rural outdoor fires, safety clearances, burn pile limits, and emergency fire bans across the township.

byLaws.title: Animal Care & Leash By-law
byLaws.summary: Sets mandatory pet licensing, maximum 2m leash length on public grounds, stoop-and-scoop requirements, and dangerous dog classifications.

guides.title: Comprehensive Municipal Permit, Required Documents & 311 Service Request Manual
guides.description: Official municipal master guide (MW-PERMITS-311-GUIDE-2026-REV3). Comprehensive coverage of NJ UCC building permits, mandatory required documents by permit classification (decks, pools, fences, additions, tree removals, dumpsters, road cuts), and 311 citizen municipal service request intake standards (pothole reporting criteria, SLAs, 50m duplicate detection, and 4-stage tracking).

guides.title: Comprehensive Municipal Manual on Recycling, Solid Waste Disposal & Resource Recovery
guides.description: Official Department of Public Works master manual (MW-DPW-RECYCLE-2026-REV5). Comprehensive 8-chapter guide covering dual-stream recycling, 359 Boyden Ave depot operations, bulk drop-off rules, leaf vacuuming, public waste enforcement (§ 209-14 illegal dumping penalties up to $2,500), broken park bin repair SLAs, refuse accumulation 48-hour abatement notices, and public garbage odor sanitization.

guides.title: 2026 Curbside Waste & Recycling Calendar
guides.description: Complete zone schedule for garbage, recycling, and green organics collection.

guides.title: Backyard Deck Construction Manual
guides.description: Illustrated guide to setbacks, spans, footing depth, and building code standards.

guides.title: Residential Pool Safety & Enclosure Handbook
guides.description: Clear guidelines for 1.5m fencing, gate hardware, and site inspection prep.

guides.title: Town of Maplewood New Resident Welcome Kit
guides.description: Everything new residents need to know about municipal services, taxes, and bylaws.

serviceRequests.portalDescription: Submit, track, and resolve non-emergency municipal service requests online. Connect directly with Public Works, Roads, Parks, Waste, and By-law enforcement crews.
serviceRequests.emergencyNotice: For life-threatening emergencies call 911 immediately. For active water main breaks call (555) 123-9287. For downed power lines call 1-800-434-1235.
